question.problem: Given that $\text{Cov}[X,Y]=-3,$ $\text{SD}[X]=3,$ and $\text{SD}[Y]=2$, find the correlation coefficient of the random variables $X$ and $Y.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the correlation coefficient of the random variables $X$ and $Y$ is defined as

$$
\rho =\frac{\text{Cov}[X,Y]}{\text{SD}[X]\cdot \text{SD}[Y]},
$$

where

- $\text{Cov}[X,Y]$ is the covariance, and

- $\text{SD}[X]$ and $\text{SD}[Y]$ are the standard deviations of $X$ and $Y.$

Substituting our data in the formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\rho  & =\frac{\text{Cov}[X,Y]}{\text{SD}[X]\cdot \text{SD}[Y]} \\  & =\frac{-3}{3\cdot 2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
